purpose: Identify and constrain an untouched empirical twilight-radiance source before opening target radiance values, preserving the separation between surrogate-vs-MYSTIC validation and MYSTIC/atmosphere-vs-real-sky validation.

pgnL1SemanticsReference.blickManualEvidence: Level 1 data type metadata distinguishes 1=corrected count rate, 2=radiance [W/m2/nm/sr], 3=irradiance [W/m2/nm]

publicArchive.rawAndCorrectedDataPolicy: PGN archives L0 raw field spectra and L1 data after instrument-characteristic corrections; L1 is not assumed to be absolute radiance unless its own metadata says data type 2

instrumentEvidence.instrumentFamily: Pandora-2S inferred from paired s1/s2 archive identity and subject to exact calibration-file confirmation

beforeAnyTargetRadianceOpening: verify through PGN metadata/API that exact Pandora209 s1+s2 calibration records apply to the selected session

verify from L1 metadata that every strict-validation spectrum has Level 1 data type 2=radiance with W/m2/nm/sr units; reject corrected-count-rate type 1 and irradiance type 3 for this directional-radiance target
verify exact uncertainty representation for both spectrometers
enumerate session/file identities using metadata only and confirm twilight zenith or otherwise preregistered pointing coverage
freeze a deterministic overlap/stitch rule for the two spectrometers without inspecting sky-radiance values
freeze independent AOD source hierarchy, uncertainty propagation, and maximum temporal separation/stability rule
freeze cloud/glare QC sources and synchronization rule using SONA/BSRN/AERONET or other independent site evidence
freeze immutable raw-file hashing and session split before target values are read
freeze comparison metrics and pass/fail gates before target values are read

otherCandidates.reason: Strong zenith-twilight spectral calibration and collocated AERONET/MPLNET evidence, but the paper explicitly states that ResPan data are not publicly accessible and model/experimental data are incomplete or subject to change; published radiance/model comparisons are already open and therefore should not be treated as an untouched final validation holdout.

Absolute twilight photometry and large archival sample are useful for sanity checks, but the published dataset is already open and does not supply a frozen independent per-observation AOD/QC package matching the strict admission contract.

Absolute directional photopic measurements are valuable for order-of-magnitude and geometry checks, but modern independent aerosol characterization, immutable digital raw provenance, and session-level QC are unavailable.
Measurements were reported in arbitrary units with reconstruction/renormalization from measurement fragments; this does not meet the absolute-calibration requirement for strict radiance validation.
TEMPO provides calibrated twilight Earth radiances, but its satellite viewing geometry is not the ground-based directional sky-radiance geometry used by the star-visibility model.

nextSafeTransition.action: metadata-only PGN/AERONET/IZO session-universe construction and pre-value contract freeze
